minimum_boundary_cases: Positive control: sandbox reads known owned marker and writes a new owned file with exact expected bytes. Trusted parent verifies output and unchanged outside-marker hashes.

Read/write denial: oracle and other-arm markers reject direct path, parent traversal, symlink and inherited-descriptor routes; blocked bytes never appear in sandbox stdout. Pass only on expected access-denial outcomes, not arbitrary process/setup failure.

Network control: trusted parent starts an owned loopback sentinel, proves it reachable outside sandbox, then sandbox connection to that listener must fail within1second; no external endpoint/DNS/model request. This proves the tested route only.

Process cleanup: owned child/grandchild and a setsid-attempt child record PIDs/start-times; force watchdog expiry, TERM then KILL with frozen grace, reap and assert every recorded descendant is gone and owned namespace/endpoint no longer reachable.

If escaped descendants cannot be contained and cleaned within the owned boundary, fail and preserve evidence; do not kill unrelated processes or assert all-descendant confinement from leader timeout alone.

Negative controls: independently remove one read restriction, network restriction and cleanup obligation in isolated owned configurations; each corresponding assertion must reject its planted breach. Never weaken the real profile or shared host.
